result.summary:
I rewrote the route data for plates p03 (tassels) and p04 (landing) to follow ARCHITECTURE.md §5. Both files load in Node, keep the schema and no longer have `draft: true`. I checked them three ways: the repo's plate-overlay tool (plain, `--approved` and `--clean`), my own renderer that applies the occluders the way the game does, and side-by-side comparisons with the approved screenshots.

**p03 (tassels)**
- **Purl's path:** 11 points from the camera up the central carpet to the round landing, then a short turn right on the landing's shallow top (y≈868–905). The exit points right, toward the landing's right post.
- **Stop:** at f=0.030, readyF=0. Purl stands at (411,1514) with width 294, exactly the approved spot.
- **Widths and lanes:** widths shrink with the measured carpet width (about 0.535 × carpet width). Lanes go from 118 down to 0. Lanes −1, 0 and +1 and the whole sprite stay between the gold rails at every depth.
- **Teal pickup:** f=0.894 at (359,887), size 71 (the approved size).
- **Tassels:** stored as top anchors at y 390, 480 and 583 (approved bottoms minus w×498/319). Lifts of 170, 260 and 363 raise all three tops to y 220, just under the upper beam. Raised bottoms end up at about 490–496, more than 250 px above Purl's highest head on the landing, even mid-jump.
- **Loop's path:** he starts on the right teal bridge behind the lantern post and passes his approved spot exactly ((722,972), width 117). He then shrinks to width 85 and disappears behind the central tower. He has a stitch task at f 0.35 (sparkle at 772,952) and a teal pickup at f 0.65 (size 48).
- **Occluders:**
  - `lantern` covers Loop as he enters at the right edge.
  - `tower` starts at y 858, just below the lowered right tassel, so redrawing the tower never erases tassel pixels. My first version did cut that tassel in half.
- **Wipe column:** the central tower, x 478–576.

**p04 (landing)**
- **Purl's path:** 9 points. It starts at the approved 04 spot ((450,1458), width 313; target 450,1455,312), passes the approved 05 spot within 3 px (296 vs 301 wide), runs up the broad landing beside the big left tower, and turns right along the carpet's bend below the far rail's braid.
- **Lanes:** 130 near the camera, 0 at the exit, all on carpet.
- **Events:**
  - The `hint` event is at f=0 with the requested text, stored as \u escapes so file encoding can't garble it.
  - `loopReturn` is at f 0.02.
  - `reveal` is at f 0.245, where Purl is at (445,1288) with Snagling ahead-left.
  - `exit` is at f=1.
- **Drops:** for any contact in the window, a drop at f+0.10 in lane +1 lands at about (558–568, 1190–1215), ahead-right on carpet with wide lanes (about 95–105).
- **Snagling:** the hidden pose (92,1235, width 165) sits entirely inside the `left-tower` occluder (behindY 1300). I checked this with the peek, idle, alert and reach frames. The peek pose (205,1270, width 202) is then partly behind the tower edge, so he reads as peeking out from behind it.
- **Loop's path:** he climbs the rising bridge from the right edge to the platform on top of the column, passing his approved 04 spot exactly. He has a hop task at f 0.33 (703,590).
- **Camera and wipe:** I lowered `zMax` to 1.6 so the left tower stays in view at the reveal (zoom is about 1.3–1.45 there). The wipe column is the left tower, x 0–180.
verification: Both files pass `node --check` and load through core/ww.js and core/path.js. A script confirmed the required keys are present, there is no draft flag, every event f is in [0,1], Purl points have 4 values and Loop points have 3.

Approved positions, measured with WW.path.project and sample. p03 stop sample: (411.0,1514.2), width 294.1 (approved 411,1514,294). p03 Loop: (722,972), width 117, exact. p04 start: (450,1458), width 313 (approved 450,1455,312). p04 at the approved 05 Purl spot: 2.8 px away, width −1.7%. p04 Loop at the 04 spot: exact.
Ran tools/plate-overlay.py for p03 and p04 in plain, --approved and --clean modes and looked at every result.

My own renderer (draws sprites in depth order and repaints plate pixels for occluders, like the game) showed: lanes −1/0/+1 on carpet at several f values on both plates; lifted tassels clear of Purl; Loop's p03 entry behind the lantern and exit behind the tower, with the lowered tassel left intact; Snagling's hidden pose fully covered and the peek pose partly out; p04 drops landing ahead-right on carpet.
Side-by-side images of the approved 03, 04 and 05 screenshots next to my data rendered on the clean plates: Purl, Loop, tassels and spool line up visually.
openIssues: Reveal timing depends on the landing length the level.js author picks, which I don't own. My reveal at f=0.245 gives about 1.5 s of running only if the landing length is at least 30 m (≈1.2 s at 25 m, ≈2 s at 40 m). Recommendation: landing length 30–40 m.

Visual speed: p04's path is only 2.52 racer-widths long (p03 is 4.61; p01 as authored is 8.76) because the landing is compact. At the 30–40 m needed for the Snagling encounter, Purl crosses this plate on screen noticeably slower than on p01. The level author or renderer may want to account for this; the run cycle is tied to metres, not pixels.

Loop's approved 05 spot (634,531, width 95) is only approximated: the closest point on his path is 16.6 px away and 11.6% wider. I matched the 04 spot exactly; hitting both would need a sharp kink and a sudden size drop.

The p03 teal spool keeps the approved size of 71. By the time Purl reaches it on the landing (width about 100), the spool is about as tall as he is. This matches the approved art's stylization, but the renderer may choose to draw it smaller in close-up.

Loop's path start points (p03 at 838,1130; p04 at 838,662) put part of his sprite beyond x=841, so he walks in from the plate edge. The renderer should clip world drawing to the plate rectangle; otherwise, on wide screens he shows briefly in the blurred framing area. On p03 his tuft also peeks over the lantern at f≈0, which looks physically right.

Snagling at the peek pose is half behind the left tower (face visible), so he reads as peeking. In the approved 04 art he is drawn slightly in front of the tower edge. If the renderer wants him fully visible at the peek, it can ignore the occluder for him once the reveal starts. Lowering behindY would instead make him pop in front of the tower partway through his hop.

Occluders were tested only with my own Pillow renderer, not the real game renderer, which doesn't exist yet. The p03 `tower` occluder is shaped (y ≥ 858) so that redrawing the whole polygon still never erases a lowered tassel.
When Purl stops in lane +1 on p03, his sprite covers the plate's painted stitch ring at (571,1365). The renderer's cue layer (pulsing ring and pill, drawn above actors) keeps the tap target visible.

result.summary:
I replaced the draft route data for plates p01 (ribbon) and p02 (shortcut) with traced geometry that follows ARCHITECTURE.md §5. Both files keep the schema, have no `draft` key and load in Node with every other plate. Only these two files were edited.

**p01 (ribbon)**
- **Purl's path** (12 points, 8.54 widths long) starts on the lower coral carpet. It goes up through the twist where the carpet turns into the ribbon, up-left along the lower band, round the turn at upper left, then right along the upper band. It ends at the ribbon's top-right curl next to the central tower (466,594).
- **Purl's size and lanes**: Purl shrinks from 293 to 95 px wide as the route goes up. Lane spacing is 100 px at the start and drops to 0 at the twist.
- **Composition**: the start (f=0) is 14 px from Purl's approved spot. The stop (f=0.006, readyF 0) is 0.7 px away and 1.1% narrower than the approved Purl.
- **Coral spool**: picked up at f=0.83 on the upper band, at (328,620), size 62.
- **ribbon.band**: runs from the carpet's far edge (y 1132) up to the curl, covering the walkable surface and the twist.
- **Loop**: starts exactly at his approved spot (726,1068, width 145) and climbs the teal ribbon until he is behind the tower. His stitch task is at f=0.02 with its sparkle at (636,1108); his coral pickup is at f=0.6, size 60.
- **Occluders**: the near-left railing post hides Purl's left side when he runs in lane −1. The tower trunk hides Loop at the end of his route.
- **Wipe column**: the central tower, x 345–560.

**p02 (shortcut)**
- **Purl's path** (8 points, 3.68 widths) starts on the broad landing. There is a control point on the stop, so the stop (f=0.057) lands 0.4 px from the approved spot at the same width (292). The start (f=0) is 62 px further back to give him a short run-in.
- **Runner and exit**: the path goes up the runner, which narrows from 292 to 104 px. Lanes stay on the runner and drop to 0 near the roll. Purl ends in front of the cream roll, bending right towards the right tower (exit f=1).
- **Teal preview spool**: the path never comes closer than 247 px to it.
- **shortcut.band**: runs from the landing's far edge (y 1338) to the bottom of the plate's roll (465,936), half-width 124.
- **Preview and cameo**: the teal preview is at (405,724), size 65. The Snagling cameo is at (211,742), width 130, matching the approved positions.
- **Loop**: runs in from the right edge along the bypass and passes his approved spot (717,687, width 111) exactly. His bypass task (extra 3.5 s) is at f=0.97, where he is already hidden.
- **Occluders**: the big plum tassel and the railing posts at the bypass's upper-left end hide Loop. Neither ever covers Purl.
- **Wipe column**: the right tower, x 575–705.

I checked everything with the overlay tool (normal, approved and clean modes), my own band/occluder renderer, enlarged crops and a Node script. Sprites stand on the carpet, lanes stay on walkable ground, and occluders hide only what they should. The sim, renderer and camera have not been tested with this data because those modules didn't exist yet.
verification: Node load test: all six plate files load together with core/ww.js, core/path.js and asset-data.js; WW.PLATES.p01 and p02 have no draft key; every event f is within [0,1].

Projection check (tools/check.js in my scratchpad): p01 stop f=0.006 lands at (273.9,1517.3) with w 285.7, against the approved (274,1518,289); p01 start is 14.1 px away. p02 stop f=0.057 lands at (346.0,1530.4) with w 292.0, against the approved (346,1530,292). Zoom at the stop is 1.026 on p01 and 1.020 on p02.
Loop's approved positions: p01 f=0 is exactly (726,1068,145); p02 passes exactly (717,687,111) at f=0.433.

Occluder check by sampling sprite boxes against the polygons with the behindY rule: on p01 the left post hides Purl only in lane −1 for f 0.040–0.105 and never hides Loop; the tower hides only Loop (f ≥ 0.635). On p02 the big tassel and corner posts hide only Loop (f ≥ 0.52) and never Purl.
The teal preview spool on p02 is never closer than 247 px to Purl's path, so it cannot be reached there.
Ran tools/plate-overlay.py on p01 and p02 in default, --approved and --clean modes. Looked at the results: the stop sprites line up with the approved Purl and Loop line up with his approved spot.

Rendered enlarged crops with occlusion applied and checked them by eye: the climb around the p01 turn, Loop going behind the p01 tower, Purl in lane −1 behind the p01 left post, Purl running up the p02 runner to the roll, and Loop on the p02 bypass disappearing behind the tassel and posts.
Not verified: behaviour in the actual sim, renderer and camera, which did not exist yet. Nothing was run on an Android device.
openIssues: Band half-widths: I measured the half-width in ribbon.band and shortcut.band perpendicular to the band's centre line, which is not stated in ARCHITECTURE.md. tools/plate-overlay.py draws the band as horizontal ticks instead. p01's upper ribbon runs almost horizontally, so a renderer that offsets the band horizontally would collapse it to a line there. The renderer should offset along the band's normal.

Coral spool position: the spool is drawn on Purl's centre line at (328,620). The approved image places it on the far edge of the upper band at (315,575), so in the game it sits about 45 px lower and 13 px to the right. The pickup schema has no x/y override; moving the path onto the far edge to match would put Purl's feet on that edge.

Segment lengths for level.js: Purl's paths are 8.54 widths (p01) and 3.68 widths (p02); Loop's are 2.69 (p01) and 3.51 (p02). If segment lengths in metres are not roughly proportional to these, racers will appear to skate or run in place on screen. In particular, Loop's p01 route is short on screen because of where the teal ribbon is in the art.

Loop starts off the plate on p02: his path begins at x=880, past the plate's right edge at 841, so he runs in from off-screen. The renderer should clip world sprites to the plate rectangle, or he will show over the blurred framing on wide screens. This is only a few pixels on phones.

p02 Snagling cameo: the approved image uses snagling atlas frame 0, which is snag.idle in the runtime frames. ARCHITECTURE.md says the cameo is a 'peek'. Drawing snag.peek at width 130 gives a shorter, different-looking Snagling. Use snag.idle at (211,742, width 130) to match the approved image.

Exits and connector style: p01 ends at the ribbon's top-right curl against the central tower, and p02 ends in front of the roll bending right towards the right tower. Neither plate shows walkable ground beyond its exit, so the connector wipe has to carry Purl 'around the tower'. Suggested connector style is 'right' for both c-ribbon and c-shortcut.

Purl's on-screen size: with zMax at the contract's 1.8, Purl appears about 171 px wide (design scale) at the top of the p01 ribbon, against 293 at the start, so his size is not constant there. I kept 1.8; raising it would keep him larger but make the plate noticeably softer.

Ghosted ribbon before opening: the ribbon band covers the walkable surface and the lower twist. The cream underside below the upper curl (around x 240–500, y 640–800) is outside the band and stays solid when the band is ghosted. The plate's own cream roll on p02 also stays visible while the roll sprite starts at the near end, so two rolls show at once unless the renderer handles it.
p01 stop is very close to the start: it is only about 15 px (f 0.006) ahead of f=0 so that both match the approved composition. On GO, Purl moves only a few pixels before halting at the stitch.
